proof_summary: Gamma duplication and shift formulas rewrite the terms as a quotient of ordinary factorials and an odd arithmetic-progression product; removing the factors divisible by $p$ and splitting the remaining products into residue blocks modulo $p^r$ reduces the successive-term ratio to shifted unit products, with a Morley-type parity identity handling the half-integer product.  Pairing and permuting residues gives $\sum u^{-1}=O(p^{2r})$ and $\sum u^{-2}=O(p^r)$, so a second-order product expansion makes every required block $1+O(p^{3r})$; the resulting $p$-adic estimate, together with integrality, yields the divisibility of the difference.
